title: Keep authorized Case picker selectors reopenable in Investigation Timeline
goal: Close the read-only Case Queue -> Investigation Timeline selector trust-boundary mismatch. Reuse one Case ID predicate so no authorized catalog entry may be published if the destination Timeline HTTP handler must reject it.
invariants: No Case catalog candidate may appear in a discovery response if the same ID would fail the Case Timeline HTTP selector boundary.
Case and source read authorization remain separately enforced by the existing first-party owner checker.
No new IAM, Case mutation, database, source exposure or provenance semantics.
security_properties: Reject NUL/CR/LF owner-catalog Case identifiers with the same canonical predicate as direct Timeline selection.
Fail closed before any candidate Case ACL enumeration or partially authorized Case list is serialized.

migration.rationale: Read-only HTTP selection consistency; no persisted canonical object changes.

rollback.strategy: Revert the shared selector reuse without changing canonical owner ACLs.
verification: Canonical read-only picker and Timeline behaviors unaffected for ordinary Case IDs.

inputs: Existing source-owned Case discovery and Timeline GET paths.
Canonical CAP-INV-110 navigation and CAP-INV-101 Case opening contract.
outputs: One common selector predicate reused by picker and Timeline.
Behavioral tests that malformed provider IDs produce generic errors without partial enumeration.
acceptance_tests: Authorized Case remains openable and owner checks still run.
NUL, CR and LF in any Case candidate block all picker results and do not invoke ACL checks.
Direct Timeline HTTP refuses identical invalid IDs.
Exact SHA mandatory Actions verified before any integration.

performance_budget.rationale: One O(n) bounded Case ID validation at an existing authorization boundary; no new data traversal.

definition_of_ready: Existing E10-INV-110E verified in engineering foundation graph; this is an independent bounded read-only security compatibility fix.
Frozen PR #36 base is not mutated.
definition_of_done: Code published on child branch with exact SHA and no mutable parent.
Negative and authorized positive paths verified by GitHub Actions, no required gate waived.
Security and integration limitations handed off, unit not claimed production accepted.
